From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Mar 2028 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarifications on audit-log preservation / export mechanics

Marcus / Naomi,

Draft below is tuned for Meadowbank's ask. I kept it short but technically specific. Please edit before Marcus sends externally.

--Draft Answer--
1) Export formats & sample layout
  - Supported formats: compressed NDJSON (.ndjson.gz), Parquet (.parquet), and gzipped CSV for legacy clients.
  - Schema: each event exported as a top-level JSON object with these canonical fields: timestamp_iso8601, event_id (UUID v4), user_id (hashed optional), action, resource_type, resource_id, request_payload_schema_version, response_code, shard_id, server_hostname, sequence_number.
  - Partitioning & packaging: Exports are partitioned by day then by shard (e.g., 2028-02-01/shard-03/*.ndjson.gz) and delivered as a single envelope tar.gz containing per-day folders. Parquet exports are stored as date=YYYY-MM-DD/parquet-files with _metadata describing schema.
  - Sample: attaching an NDJSON sample (export-sample-2028-03-01.ndjson).

2) Preservation metadata & tamper evidence
  - Checksums: We include file-level SHA-256 checksums for every artifact and a manifest.json that lists file paths, sizes, and checksums.
  - Signed manifest: For preservation handoffs we sign the manifest with Redwood's preservation signing key (RSA-4096 currently). Signature and signing-cert (X.509) are included in the envelope.
  - Timestamps: All exported events include server-generated ISO8601 timestamps and we include an export-generated timestamp (UTC) recorded in the manifest.
  - Chain-of-custody: Manifest includes exporter user id, export job id, and UTC start/end times. We log export job activity (who requested, IP, job parameters) and those entries are stored as part of the export bundle.

3) Delivery options & integrity verification
  - Delivery: S3 (bucket-to-bucket transfer or pre-signed URLs), encrypted HTTPS endpoint push, or staged retrieval via a secure file share (SFTP with key auth).
  - Encryption: Exports are AES-256 encrypted at rest. We can envelope with a customer-provided KMS key for hosted/dedicated customers.
  - Verification: Recipient validates file checksums against manifest and can validate the manifest signature against the X.509 cert we provide.

4) SLA & lead time estimates (30 days / ~100M events)
  - Standard lead time: 3-5 business days for up to 10M events (hosted).
  - Bulk extraction: For ~100M events (30-day window) we estimate 7-10 business days, subject to queuing and mutually agreed maintenance windows. Dedicated customers with reserved export bandwidth can reduce this to 2-4 business days.
  - Expedite: Emergency legal-hold exports can be escalated; typical expedited turnaround is 48-72 hours with an operations fee and signed escalation.

5) Legal hold & preservation freeze
  - We support placing data on a preservation freeze: once a legal-hold flag is set for an account, data is retained and immutable for the hold duration. Exports created under legal hold include the hold identifier and tamper-evident manifest.
  - Auditability: Export jobs and hold changes are tracked in our audit trail with immutable timestamps and are included in evidence bundles.

6) Caveats & PII considerations
  - If you require automated PII redaction, we provide tokenization/field-masking options, but note that redaction may remove fields necessary for certain investigations. We recommend a narrow redaction policy for legal-preservation exports.
  - Retention policy: Hosts default retention is configurable per-customer; we can provide a retention matrix showing default retention + tiering (hot/archival).

--End Draft--

Naomi: anything to add on chain-of-custody logging or for dedicated export bandwidth guarantees?

Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Regina / Tom,

Thanks for the follow-ups. Below is a consolidated technical response from our preservation team (copied Laura + Naomi). I've also attached a short preservation summary and a tiny NDJSON sample so you can validate schema and checksum flow.

Quick highlights:
- Supported export formats: NDJSON (ndjson.gz), Parquet, CSV (gz) 
- Preservation: SHA-256 per-file, manifest.json with file metadata, RSA-4096-signed manifest + X.509 cert included in envelope
- Delivery: S3 (bucket transfer or pre-signed), HTTPS push, or SFTP; AES-256 at rest; optional customer KMS
- Lead time for ~100M events (30 days): estimated 7-10 business days (2-4 days for Dedicated customers with reserved bandwidth).
- Chain-of-custody: export job logs (requester, job id, IP, timestamps) are included and immutable in the evidence bundle

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred delivery method (S3 presigned vs. HTTPS push) and whether you require customer KMS.
2) If Meadowbank needs a legal-hold preservation bundle with expedited SLA, indicate and we'll scope an expedited plan (48-72h target subject to ops fee).
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week to review the sample and manifest verification steps.

If you want a one-pager we can hand to your legal team, Laura's preservation summary (attached) is suitable.

Best,
